intended_object: The composition F ∘ G of two type constructors (applicative functors on types), meaning the type F (G α). The docstring and the `Functor`/`Applicative` instances built on it in `Mathlib/Control/Functor.lean` show this.
explanation: The body `F <| G α` is just the composite type constructor applied to α. This is the object part of the composite of two endofunctors on `Type`. The universe levels are fully general (`Type v → Type u` and `Type u → Type w`), so the definition is not too narrow. Using a separate name instead of `Function.comp` is a deliberate choice, explained in the docstring, so that type class resolution does not get confused. It does not change what the construction means. The Functor, Applicative and LawfulApplicative instances defined on it later in the file give it the structure of a composition of functors. Mathlib has no other definition of this exact type-level functor composition. The general category-theory `CategoryTheory.Functor.comp` lives in a different framework, and this definition is not a special case written out by hand.
